A useful hint connects a student's attempt to the idea you have just taught.
Try these activities to see how a lesson explanation can guide the advice.
**Check** tests the answer; **Feedback** helps the student decide what to try next.

## Automatic section context

Place the explanation you want students to use directly before the activity.
Feedback can then refer to that explanation. Start a new heading when you move
to another idea. For a definition reused in several places, choose a named
passage as shown later on this page.

::: {.callout-note title="Remember the discriminant"}
For $ax^2+bx+c=0$, the discriminant is $D=b^2-4ac$. Its sign tells us how many
real roots the equation has. Use this rule in the question below.
:::

```{math-exercise}
#| label: ai-auto-context
#| vars: a,b,c
#| field-labels: Discriminant
For $2x^2+3x-2=0$, compute the discriminant: _[25]
```

## Reusable explicit context

Use one explanation in several questions without repeating it. Give the passage
a name, then select that name in each exercise. Both questions below use the
same reminder about Newton's method. Open their source to see how.

::: {#newton-rule .math-exercise-context}
::: {.callout-tip title="Explicit feedback context: Newton's method"}
Newton's method uses
$x_{k+1}=x_k-f(x_k)/f'(x_k)$. Evaluate the function and derivative at the
current iterate before forming the next iterate.
:::
:::

<details class="math-example-source">
<summary>Show context-block source</summary>

```markdown
::: {#newton-rule .math-exercise-context}
Newton's method uses
$x_{k+1}=x_k-f(x_k)/f'(x_k)$. Evaluate the function and derivative at the
current iterate before forming the next iterate.
:::
```

</details>

```{math-exercise}
#| label: ai-explicit-context
#| context: newton-rule
#| mode: numeric
#| tolerance: 0.001
For $f(x)=x^2-2$ and $x_0=1.5$, compute $x_1$: _[17/12]
```

## Several exercises sharing one context

```{math-exercise}
#| label: ai-explicit-context-second
#| context: newton-rule
#| vars: x
For $f(x)=x^3-1$, write the Newton update as a function of $x_k$:
__[x-(x^3-1)/(3*x^2)]
```

## Opting out of context

Use `context: none` when surrounding prose should not be sent with a feedback
request. This disables both automatic collection and accidental inheritance
from the current section.

```{math-exercise}
#| label: ai-no-context
#| context: none
Compute $12/3$: _[4]
```

## Multi-field feedback

Meaningful labels make hints clearer and prevent generic references such as
“field 2”.

```{math-exercise}
#| label: ai-field-labels
#| vars: x
#| field-labels: Derivative, Value at x=2, Tangent slope
For $f(x)=x^3$, enter $f'(x)=$ _[3*x^2], $f'(2)=$ _[12], and the slope of the
tangent at $x=2$: _[12].
```

## Mathematics in AI context

Feedback can refer to the same formulas students see in the lesson. Here the
notation for a solenoid gives students the definitions they need for the task.

::: {#solenoid-notation .math-exercise-context}
A long solenoid has $N$ turns over a length $l$. Its turn density is
$n=\frac{N}{l}$, measured in $\mathrm{m}^{-1}$. In vacuum,
$\mu_0\approx 4\pi\times10^{-7}\,\mathrm{H/m}$.
For radius $2a$, the ideal long-solenoid approximation gives

$$
L=\frac{4\pi\mu_0N^2a^2}{l}.
$$
:::

```{math-exercise}
#| label: ai-solenoid-source
#| caption: Turn density
#| context: solenoid-notation
#| vars: N,l
#| field-labels: Turn density
Write the turn density in terms of $N$ and $l$: _[N/l]
```

Ask for feedback and notice whether it uses the notation from the explanation.
This is especially useful when a course introduces unfamiliar symbols.

[More ways to guide feedback](https://github.com/Erasmus-CTM/math-exercise/blob/feature/shared-feedback-integration/docs/authoring.md).
